releases.title: Clean recovery when a provider pauses
releases.summary: StatsKey now preserves completed workspace work and ends the active pass cleanly when a model provider reaches its response deadline.
highlights: A provider deadline no longer restarts the same failed autonomous pass.
Completed files, checkpoints, and verification remain saved for a clean continuation.
Managed Kimi now uses bounded requests, provider timeouts, and server-authoritative credit reservations.
Stripe billing and third-party connector authorization now use the hardened live backend.

releases.title: Work that stays with its workspace
releases.summary: StatsKey now keeps active tasks bound to the workspace where they started, while bringing billing, provider access, and third-party tools into one clearer setup.
highlights: Active tasks continue against their original workspace when you switch tabs, folders, or projects.
Execute mode can run independent work concurrently while serializing only conflicting edits.
Connections & billing centralizes Stripe, Google, GitHub, model providers, and OAuth or MCP tools.
Model selection explains pricing, adds ChatGPT Fast and Kimi, and accepts any model returned by a connected provider.

releases.title: Windows, tested where it runs
releases.summary: The Windows preview now passes a native install, launch, restart, workspace, terminal, browser, and update-readiness gate before it can be published.
highlights: Workspace changes remain available after restarting the Windows app.
Commands, installed apps, and Android tools follow the Windows environment automatically.
The release process binds the public installer to native Windows test evidence.
Completion stays tied to saved results and successful verification.

releases.title: Proof you can inspect
releases.summary: StatsKey can now exercise mobile work directly and only calls implementation complete when the saved result and its verification agree.
highlights: Simulator Lab can discover, start, inspect, and interact with iOS Simulators and Android emulators.
Completed workspace changes include persisted-change and verification evidence you can review.
Files, search, browser tabs, and workspace navigation are easier to find and use.
Long-running work settles reliably in the background and keeps its final verification visible.

releases.title: Desktop preview
releases.summary: The first public StatsKey workspace preview.
highlights: Project workspaces, local tools, model choices, and update delivery.
A conversational work log with review preferences and resumable sessions.
